[In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Targeted provision]{.layer-badge} [Pub. L. 119-75](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/119/public/75){.cite} [140 Stat. 539](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/140/539){.cite}

Bars the use of foreign assistance funds to finance assistance directly to the government of a country whose duly elected head of government is deposed by a military coup or decree, or by a coup or decree in which the military plays a decisive role. Aid may resume when the Secretary of State certifies that a democratically elected government has taken office.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: Pub. L. 119-75](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/119/public/75){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Sec. 7008(a): the prohibition, covering funds in Titles III through VI of the act, including security assistance.
- Exceptions for assistance to promote democratic elections, public participation in democratic processes, or a democratic transition, with prior consultation with the Appropriations Committees.
- Resumption on certification by the Secretary of State that a democratically elected government has taken office.
- Sec. 7008(b) (FY2026): the Secretary may waive the restriction program by program on certifying that a waiver is in the national security interest.

## Why it matters

The restriction is triggered by the facts, but in practice by a formal determination that a coup occurred, which makes the determination itself a recurring oversight question. Administrations have at times avoided one, as with Egypt in 2013; in October 2023 the State Department determined that the July takeover in Niger was a coup and suspended most assistance under this section. It reaches programs funded through the State-foreign operations act, such as [Foreign Military Financing](fmf.qmd) and [IMET](imet.qmd), but not Defense Department authorities such as [Title 10 security cooperation](seccoop-2016.qmd) unless a separate law applies.

## Current status

Re-enacted each year in the State-foreign operations appropriations act; cited here as enacted for fiscal year 2026, which includes a program-by-program waiver. Check current status.
